plan: My private value is $24. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. If I bid less than $24, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. The worst-case scenario is paying close to my value and not gaining profit. Therefore, I'll bid my true value of $24, which maximizes my potential profit across potential opponent bid scenarios.

My value is $9. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. However, I need to consider potential opponent behaviors. Since values are randomly drawn, I can't predict their exact values. Bidding exactly $9 leaves me vulnerable if others bid higher. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances while protecting downside risk.

My private value is $13. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when my value exceeds the winning bid. If I bid more, I risk paying more than my value if I win. With only one round and no prior history, bidding $13 minimizes my potential downside while maximizing my chance of winning at a fair price.
